config.title: Notification Context

intro.title: Notification Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system for a React app using the Context API. You will learn how to create a central place to manage notification messages, like success alerts or error warnings, and make them available to any component in your app. The core concept is React Context, which allows you to share state globally without passing props down manually. You'll use TypeScript to define types for your notifications and context, ensuring your code is type-safe. By the end, you'll have a working context that can display notifications from anywhere in your application.
intro.usecase: Notification Context is a fundamental pattern used across modern web applications to manage and display user notifications consistently. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon, it powers the toast messages that confirm when items are added to your cart. Dashboard applications like GitHub use it to show success or error alerts after API operations. This pattern ensures notifications appear in a standardized location and style throughout the entire application, whether they're form validation errors, payment confirmations, or system status updates.

objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of notification objects with required properties.
Use the createContext function from React to initialize a new NotificationContext.
Implement a custom NotificationProvider component to wrap application sections that need notification access.
Define useState hooks to manage arrays of notification objects as React state.
Construct handler functions to add new notifications to the state array with unique identifiers.
Execute conditional logic to remove notifications from state after a specified timeout duration.
Utilize the useContext hook to access notification state and handlers within child components.
Control component rendering by mapping through the notification array to display each notification.
Assign proper TypeScript types to context values to ensure type safety throughout the application.
Invoke notification functions from UI event handlers to trigger notification displays.
Return JSX elements from the NotificationProvider that include both children and notification displays.
Modify existing components to integrate with the notification context instead of local state.

steps.title: Import React and createContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the createContext function from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and createContext from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and createContext
import React, { createContext } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and createContext from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and createContext is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code should include an import statement that imports React and createContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and createContext. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the ability to create context providers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and createContext from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and createContext from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Import useState and useContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import the useState and useContext hooks from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Add an import statement that brings in both hooks from the same package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing hooks from 'react'
import { useState, useContext } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have both useState and useContext available from the 'react' package.
successCriteria: The import statement correctly imports both useState and useContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported both useState and useContext hooks from React.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both useState and useContext from 'react' in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both useState and useContext from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define the Notification interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named Notification with three properties: id (string), message (string), and type (string). Place this interface definition after the imports.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a Notification interface with the required properties defined.
successCriteria: The code must include a TypeScript interface named Notification with id: string, message: string, and type: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Notification interface with all required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you've defined all three properties (id, message, type) with the correct string type annotations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Notification interface is not properly defined. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all three properties with string types.

steps.title: Define the NotificationContext interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'NotificationContext' that describes the shape of the context value. It should have two properties: 'notifications' (an array of Notification objects) and 'addNotification' (a function that takes a Notification object and returns void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the two properties with their types. Remember that 'Notification' is already defined from the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a NotificationContext interface that defines the structure for the context value, enabling type safety when using the context later.
successCriteria: The interface must be named 'NotificationContext' and include both 'notifications: Notification[]' and 'addNotification: (notification: Notification) => void' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the NotificationContext interface with the correct properties and types. This will provide type safety for our context value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface needs both properties with the correct types. Make sure 'notifications' is an array of Notification objects and 'addNotification' is a function that takes a Notification and returns void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationContext interface is not correctly defined. It should have two properties: 'notifications' (an array of Notification) and 'addNotification' (a function taking Notification and returning void).

steps.title: Create the NotificationContext with createContext
steps.instruction: Create a React context called NotificationContext using the createContext function you imported. Pass undefined as the initial value and explicitly type it with the NotificationContext interface you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use the createContext function to create a context. Remember to export it so you can use it in other components.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a NotificationContext constant created with createContext, typed with NotificationContext | undefined, and initialized with undefined.
successCriteria: createContext
NotificationContext
undefined
NotificationContext interface type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully created the NotificationContext using createContext with the correct typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using createContext, naming it NotificationContext, passing undefined as the initial value, and typing it with the NotificationContext interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a context using createContext, name it NotificationContext, pass undefined as the initial value, and type it with the NotificationContext interface.

steps.title: Create the NotificationProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationProvider that takes children as props. The component should return the NotificationContext.Provider element with children as its child.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called NotificationProvider that accepts a props object with a 'children' property. Return NotificationContext.Provider with the children prop passed as its child.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationProvider component is defined that will eventually wrap the application and provide the notification context.
successCriteria: Component named NotificationProvider is defined
Accepts children prop typed as React.ReactNode
Returns NotificationContext.Provider with children as child
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the NotificationProvider component. This component will serve as the wrapper that provides notification context to your entire application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your component is named exactly 'NotificationProvider', accepts a children prop, and returns NotificationContext.Provider with the children as its child.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationProvider component isn't properly defined. Remember to create a functional component that takes children as props and returns NotificationContext.Provider with those children.

steps.title: Initialize notifications state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, initialize a state variable named 'notifications' using the useState hook. The state should be typed as an array of Notification objects (Notification[]), and initialized with an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type parameter for useState as Notification[].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing typed state with useState
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component now has a notifications state variable that is properly typed as an array of Notification objects and initialized with an empty array.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call inside the NotificationProvider component that creates a 'notifications' state variable typed as Notification[] and initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the notifications state with the correct type and initial value. This state will hold all active notifications in our context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be an issue with the type annotation or initial value. Make sure you're using useState<Notification[]>([]) to properly type the state as an array of Notification objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications state isn't properly initialized. You need to use the useState hook inside the NotificationProvider component to create a state variable named 'notifications' that's typed as Notification[] and initialized with an empty array.

steps.title: Define the addNotification function
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, define an addNotification function that takes a message and type (as an object), creates a notification object with a unique id, and updates the notifications state by adding the new notification.
steps.hint: Use the Date.now() method to generate a simple unique id. The function should accept an object with message and type properties, then use the setNotifications state setter to add the new notification to the existing array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component now has an addNotification function that can create new notifications with unique ids and add them to the notifications state array.
successCriteria:
The addNotification function should:
1. Accept an object with message and type properties
2. Generate a unique id (e.g., using Date.now().toString())
3. Create a complete Notification object with id, message, and type
4. Update the notifications state by adding the new notification to the existing array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the addNotification function. This function properly creates a new notification with a unique id and updates the state by adding it to the existing notifications array.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your addNotification function:
- Accepts an object with message and type properties
- Generates a unique id for the notification
- Creates a complete Notification object
- Properly updates the state using setNotifications
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNotification function isn't defined correctly. You need to create a function that takes message and type, generates an id, creates a notification object, and updates the notifications state.

steps.title: Create the context value object
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, create a constant named 'contextValue' that contains an object with the 'notifications' state and the 'addNotification' function.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable that holds an object with the required properties. The object should match the NotificationContext interface structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a 'contextValue' constant inside the NotificationProvider component that contains an object with 'notifications' and 'addNotification' properties.
successCriteria: The code should include a constant named 'contextValue' that is an object with 'notifications' and 'addNotification' properties, matching the NotificationContext interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the context value object that will be provided to consumers of the NotificationContext.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'contextValue' is a constant object containing both 'notifications' and 'addNotification' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context value object is missing or incomplete. Create a constant named 'contextValue' with an object containing 'notifications' and 'addNotification' properties.

steps.title: Return the NotificationContext.Provider
steps.instruction: In the NotificationProvider component, return the NotificationContext.Provider with the contextValue and children props.
steps.hint: Use the NotificationContext.Provider component and pass the contextValue as the value prop. The children prop should be rendered inside the provider.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component now returns a NotificationContext.Provider that wraps children and provides the context value.
successCriteria: The NotificationProvider component returns NotificationContext.Provider with value prop set to contextValue and renders children inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the NotificationContext.Provider, which will wrap child components and provide them with the notification context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning NotificationContext.Provider with the correct props. The provider needs a value prop and should render children inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationProvider component should return NotificationContext.Provider with the context value and children. Check that you're using the correct context name and passing the required props.

steps.title: Create a custom useNotification hook
steps.instruction: Define a custom hook named useNotification that uses useContext with NotificationContext and returns the context value.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls useContext with NotificationContext and returns the result. Make sure to handle the case where the context might be undefined.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook that provides access to the notification context with proper TypeScript typing and error handling.
successCriteria: Hook named useNotification
Uses useContext with NotificationContext
Returns the context value
Includes error handling for undefined context
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the custom useNotification hook. This will make it much easier to access notification functionality in any component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the hook 'useNotification'? Did you use useContext with NotificationContext? Did you include error handling for when the context is undefined?
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook wasn't created correctly. Remember to create a function named useNotification that calls useContext with NotificationContext and returns the context value with proper error handling.

steps.title: Export the NotificationProvider and useNotification hook
steps.instruction: Export the NotificationProvider component and the useNotification hook from this module so they can be imported and used in other files.
steps.hint: Use the 'export' keyword before the component and hook declarations, or add export statements at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component and useNotification hook are exported from this module, making them available for import in other files.
successCriteria: NotificationProvider is exported
useNotification is exported
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported both the NotificationProvider component and the useNotification hook. Now other components in your application can import and use them.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported one of the required items, but both NotificationProvider and useNotification need to be exported. Make sure both are available for import from this module.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports aren't quite right. Remember to export both the NotificationProvider component and the useNotification hook so they can be imported and used in other files.
